tasks.short: Talk with users about accounts and faults

steps.what: Report operational problems or the account fault
Read the account and the failing path
Draft a reply from the account checklist

loop.input: ticket fields and the account checklist
loop.output: reply that cites the account id or the path id
loop.check: The id in the reply is the id on the ticket
loop.stop: If both ids are missing, return an empty reply and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: The user's own wording of the block is not a checklist row

steps.what: Talk through the fault with the user
Sign the account change for this request
Apply the signed account change
Confirm the account or the path works

tasks.design: The user submits account id or path id, site and a short problem on a {HELPDESK} ticket. A bounded reply in {DOCS} uses only the account checklist and those fields. The architect still talks the fault through. A standard account change runs on the {OPS_SYSTEM} only for the signed request version. The call is not recorded or scored.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account state and the user's words lived in different mail threads, so a reply could not show which account it meant.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticket can require account id or path id, and the directory can show group and status for that id.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing what the user is actually blocked on, and odd access, still take the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides whether this is a standard account change or a fault that must stay manual.

ambition.what: Users at small sites get an account fix from the ticket without waiting for a visit

tasks.altitude: Lookup and the standard change take less time. The conversation stays. The architect can refuse a change that has no account id.

reach.task: Confirm the account or the path works
reach.learn: Which request version was signed and which problems were left open

evidence.claim: Digest [S1] and [S2] say a service desk can suggest a ticket category and draft a knowledge item for a person to review. That does not replace the user conversation.
Digest [S15] is a vendor self-service claim of fewer tickets, with no published baseline. This design does not drop the conversation on that claim.
Digest [S23] says a works council is consulted before staff monitoring. This design does not record or score the conversation.
Digest [S24] says EU AI Act high-impact duties apply if a tool rates staff. This design does not rate the user.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task covers an account check or a network fault reported by a system user. Customer needs are a different task.
Input contract: account id or path id, site, problem text, ticket id. Producer is the system user. If both ids are missing, the draft is skipped and the conversation starts from the ticket text.
The prior gives a large external share. Users here are inside the firm. The conversation stays anyway. Use the ticket form and the directory's own group fields before custom code.
Native configuration is tested first. The design does not store call recordings. If a later design did, the works council would need to be consulted.
unknowns: Which account changes are standard groups and which are exceptions.
Who may sign access when the architect is absent.
Whether the directory and the ticket share one account id.
research_questions: What share of these tickets are a known group add?
How often does the user say the first change missed the problem?

already_counted.description: Architect edits a reply that names the wrong account
Conversation time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Update the account checklist when a new standard group is added
Users resubmit a ticket that has no account id and no path id

approvals.approved_version: account change signed for this ticket id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most reports have no account id, so the checklist rarely fires and the talk does the work. The high case assumes known accounts draft cleanly, but every conversation and every nonstandard access stay manual. The visit that no longer happens is not counted as a large saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Draft and sign a network design

steps.what: Submit sites, users and constraints
Check constraints against the inventory
Draft the three network design sections

loop.input: input fields and the design template
loop.output: conceptual, logical and physical sections citing site ids
loop.check: Every site id in the draft is on the form or the gap list
loop.stop: One draft; leave a section blank if its site id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: The topology argument is not a fixed mail merge

steps.what: Decide the topology in the review
File the signed design version
Comment on the trust boundary

tasks.design: The service owner submits site, user count, sites to connect and constraints on a {WORKFLOW} form. The architect checks those fields against the {OPS_SYSTEM} inventory. A bounded draft in {DOCS} writes conceptual, logical and physical sections that cite only those fields. The architect decides the topology in review and signs one version. This task does not apply the design to live gear.
tasks.previous_blocker: Constraints arrived as mail and old drawings, so a new draft repeated a site that no longer existed.
tasks.enabler_now: Site, user count and constraint can be fields, and each can be checked against an inventory id.
tasks.still_hard: Which topology the business can live with is still a judgement, not a drawing rule.
tasks.human_edge: The architect chooses the topology and signs the version others will build from.

ambition.what: Sign a design version at each site review, not only when a project ends

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to redrawing known sites. The topology choice stays. The architect can refuse a draft that cites an unknown site.

reach.task: Comment on the trust boundary in the signed design
reach.learn: Which design version is signed and which constraints are still open

evidence.claim: A network design in a mid-size firm is a document and a review. The hard part is the topology, not the section headings.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong. That is owner, site and version, not the design argument.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so a signed design is not applied to live gear in this task.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed design version. Evaluation against a customer need, and any live build, are other tasks.
Input contract: site, user count, connected site ids, constraint text, owner. Producer is the service owner. A section with no site id is left blank.
Use the document store's own template and approval flow before custom code. The review meeting stays.
unknowns: Which sites have no inventory id.
Who may sign a design when the architect is absent.
Whether physical and logical views must be separate files.
research_questions: What share of designs cite a site that is not in the inventory?
How often does the review change the drafted topology?

already_counted.description: Architect rewrites topology prose the draft gets wrong
Topology decision time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Update the design template when a new site type appears
Security analysts add a boundary comment the template cannot know

approvals.approved_version: network design version signed in this review
the same signed network design version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes constraints arrive as free text, so the draft is thin and the review does the design. The high case assumes a clean form, but the topology decision and the sign-off still happen every time. Building the network is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge whether a design meets the need

steps.what: State the requirements the design must meet
Read the design against those requirements
Draft a gap list tied to requirement ids

loop.input: requirement ids and the reading notes
loop.output: a mark of met, weak or missing on each id
loop.check: Every mark cites a requirement id from the list
loop.stop: One pass; leave unscored any requirement with no id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a weak match is acceptable is not a fixed map

steps.what: Judge whether the design meets the need
File the signed evaluation
Hear which requirements failed

tasks.design: The customer contact submits requirement id, statement and must-or-should on a {WORKFLOW} form. The architect reads the signed design in {DOCS} against those ids. A bounded gap list marks each id met, weak or missing, and may not invent an id. The architect judges efficiency in a review and signs one evaluation. The design is not changed in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were a paragraph in mail, so an evaluation could not show which sentence it accepted or rejected.
tasks.enabler_now: Requirement id and must-or-should can be fields, and the design version can be named on the same form.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a weak match is good enough for this customer is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides if the design meets the need, and which gaps are acceptable.

ambition.what: Mark a design against requirement ids at each review, not only at handover

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to hunting for the requirement text. The judgement stays. The architect can refuse an evaluation that has no requirement id.

reach.task: Tell the customer which requirements failed
reach.learn: Which requirement ids are met, weak or missing on the signed evaluation

evidence.claim: Evaluating a design in a mid-size firm is a read against requirements and a judgement. The writing is a gap list, not a new design.
Digest [S24] says EU AI Act high-impact duties apply if a tool rates staff. This evaluation marks a design, not a person.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed evaluation of an existing design. It does not redraw the design or change the network.
Input contract: requirement id, statement, must-or-should, design version. Producer is the customer contact. A requirement with no id is listed as unscored and is not marked met.
Use the document store's comment fields before custom code. The review meeting stays because the prior is a judgement, not a checklist.
unknowns: Who writes the requirement ids when the customer sends a letter.
Which design version is the one under test.
research_questions: What share of requirements arrive with no id?
How often does the review overturn the drafted gap mark?

already_counted.description: Architect corrects a gap mark that cites the wrong paragraph
The efficiency judgement stays with the architect

incremental.description: Keep the met, weak and missing labels aligned with how reviews actually talk
Customer contacts resend a requirement that had no id

approvals.approved_version: evaluation version signed against this requirement list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requirements are still a letter, so the gap list is built by hand in the review. The high case assumes ids exist, but every efficiency judgement stays with the architect. Redrawing the design is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ask vendors and file what they answer

steps.what: List open questions from the maintenance log
Draft the question note from those rows

loop.input: question rows and the note template
loop.output: questions that each cite one question id
loop.check: Every question id in the note is on the open list
loop.stop: One draft; drop a line with no question id
loop.why_not_simpler: How to phrase a future need for this vendor is not a fixed row

steps.what: Speak with the vendor engineer
Reply with the product fact or the window
Accept or reject the vendor answer
File the accepted vendor note

tasks.design: Open questions are rows on a {WORKFLOW} list: question id, device id, need-by date. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts only those questions. The architect still talks to the vendor engineer. The reply lands on the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or by mail. The architect accepts or rejects that answer, and only the accepted version is filed. No live change is made here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vendor answers sat in mail with no question id, so the next project could not tell what had already been asked.
tasks.enabler_now: A question id can be required, and a reply can be stored against that id.
tasks.still_hard: What the firm will accept from the vendor, and the conversation itself, stay with the architect.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides which vendor answer is good enough to keep.

ambition.what: Record a vendor answer against its question in the same week, not in a later project note

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to finding the last answer. The call stays. The architect can reject an answer that cites no question id.

reach.task: Answer the open question on the shared id
reach.learn: Which question ids are still open and which answers were rejected

evidence.claim: Vendor contact in a mid-size firm is a call and a mail trail. The hard part is whether the answer is usable, not the question list.
Digest [S20] and [S21] say product cyber-resilience duties apply to products placed on the market, not to this internal maintenance conversation.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when an accepted vendor note is filed. Ordering the product and changing the network are other tasks.

Input contract: question id, device id, question text, need-by date. Producer of the question is the architect from the maintenance log. Producer of the answer is the vendor engineer. An answer with no question id is not filed.
The people-heavy prior is right. The call stays manual. Use the portal's question fields before custom code.
unknowns: Which vendors will use a portal rather than mail.
Who may accept an answer when the architect is away.
Whether a maintenance issue in the question is already on a signed window.
research_questions: What share of vendor replies cannot be tied to a question id?
How often is the first answer rejected?

already_counted.description: Architect edits a question that the log did not mean
Call time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Keep the question template aligned with new maintenance types
Vendors resend a reply that omitted the question id

approvals.approved_version: vendor answer version accepted for this question id
the same accepted vendor answer version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes replies stay as unstructured mail, so the question list does little and the call does the work. The high case assumes ids match, but every call and every accept-or-reject stays with the architect. No purchase and no live change are treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: User and vendor conversations stay. Less time goes to finding the account, the design constraint, or the last vendor answer.
reach: System users receive a filed outcome after the account conversation, not another mail round.
Information security analysts can see which design boundaries were signed and which requirements failed.
skills_to_grow: Turn a user report into an account change with a request id, or leave it as a fault with no change.
Mark each design requirement as met, weak or missing.
File a vendor answer against the question that asked it.
role.ambitious_version: Each design under review has a signed version, an evaluation against requirement ids, and a vendor note a person accepted.
